forces.title: AI consolidates consumer attention within platform environments
forces.description: AI algorithms increasingly shape consumer attention on major platforms, with over 50% of Instagram content and over 95% of TikTok watch time coming from algorithmic feeds. This structural shift moves discovery from traditional browsing to AI-driven recommendations, concentrating user engagement within these integrated environments and making brand visibility dependent on AI systems for sourcing, ranking, and recommending content.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Traditional search traffic at risk from AI-generated overviews
forces.description: The proliferation of AI-generated overviews in search results poses a significant threat to traditional open-web search traffic. More than 50% of Google searches now include AI-generated summaries, and 20-50% of traffic from the open web could be at risk by 2030. This development fundamentally alters how users access information, potentially bypassing direct visits to websites and eroding the economic model of search-dependent content platforms.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI agents driving discovery and purchase decisions
forces.description: AI agents and assistants are increasingly mediating consumer purchase decisions by ranking products, comparing alternatives, and completing transactions. This shift means 10-35% of e-commerce transactions could be initiated, influenced, or completed through AI-native experiences in the coming years. For search, social, and content platforms, integrating these agentic capabilities can create new monetization avenues and deepen their role in the consumer journey, transforming them into decision platforms.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Value shifting to integrated 'walled garden' platforms
forces.description: Value in the advertising economy is increasingly concentrating within integrated platforms, often referred to as 'walled gardens,' that bundle data, measurement, and transaction capabilities. These platforms, including major social media and video-sharing sites, are becoming decision platforms rather than just media platforms, giving them an advantage by offering advertisers closed-loop measurement and transaction visibility. This structural shift reinforces their strategic position in the new AI-driven advertising era.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Advertiser reliance on 'black box' AI optimization systems
forces.description: A key risk for advertisers is increasing reliance on 'black box optimization' systems within integrated platforms. These AI-managed systems can reduce advertiser visibility and control over ad placements and channels. With 42% of surveyed advertisers citing this as a major risk, platforms must balance advanced AI capabilities with transparency to maintain trust. This challenge impacts revenue relationships and the perceived value of ad placements on search, social, and content platforms.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Ad spend reallocation from open web to integrated platforms
forces.description: Approximately 40% of reallocated AI-driven ad spend is shifting away from traditional search and the open web towards platforms that offer stronger data, measurement, and transaction capabilities. This represents a significant structural reallocation, favoring 'walled garden' search, social, and content platforms that can provide a more integrated and measurable customer journey. The trend reinforces direct buying, bypassing traditional programmatic intermediaries and agencies.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Erosion of open web content publisher economics
forces.description: The economics of the open web and traditional content publishers are eroding as AI accelerates declining search traffic and consumers increasingly opt for AI-generated answers. Click-driven, scale-dependent publishing models are becoming unviable, with long-tail and SEO-dependent sites most exposed. This means that content platforms on the open web face significant pressure to find alternative monetization strategies beyond impression-based models, such as licensing content to AI platforms or building generative engine optimization capabilities.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI-native platforms emerging as consumer discovery channels
forces.description: New AI-native platforms like ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Claude are rapidly acquiring a growing share of consumer discovery, challenging traditional search engines and content platforms. Their conversational AI interfaces and agent layers are gaining traction due to perceived speed and utility for recommendations and synthesized answers. While these platforms currently lack mature advertising models, their privileged access to decision moments and behavioral data positions them as significant emerging competitors, potentially disrupting existing attention aggregation models.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Slowing growth in broader entertainment and media ad revenue
forces.description: The broader entertainment and media advertising revenue is experiencing a significant slowdown, with annual growth declining from 25% (2015-2020) to 12% (2021-2024). This macro trend acts as a headwind for search, social, and content platforms, as the overall pool of advertising spend they rely on is growing at a slower rate. Platforms will need to intensify efforts to capture market share and innovate monetization models amidst a less dynamic ad market.
forces.source_title: Gaming’s next growth era: Unlocking the value of attention

forces.title: Retailers reducing advertising and marketing spend
forces.description: Retailers are reducing their spending on advertising and marketing, which presents a cyclical headwind for search, social, and content platforms. As consumer confidence remains weak and trading patterns are volatile, businesses are cutting costs to protect cash and margins. This reduction in marketing budgets directly impacts the revenue streams of platforms reliant on advertising spend, requiring them to demonstrate clear ROI and value propositions to retain or attract advertiser investment.

forces.title: Opportunity for content licensing to AI platforms
forces.description: As AI platforms gain consumer discovery share, an upside driver for content platforms is the opportunity to license their content for training AI models and generating answers. This can provide a meaningful, albeit partial, offset to lost referral revenue from traditional search traffic declines. Platforms can position themselves as valuable sources of authenticated data and content for AI systems, creating new revenue streams distinct from traditional advertising and subscription models.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) for AI visibility
forces.description: Building Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) capabilities is an emerging upside driver for content platforms, enabling them to ensure visibility within AI-generated answers. As consumers increasingly rely on AI for synthesized information, optimizing content to be recognized and cited by AI models becomes critical for maintaining presence and relevance. This shift moves beyond traditional SEO, requiring platforms to adapt their content strategies to meet the evolving demands of AI-driven discovery and information retrieval.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: AI reshaping advertising value towards attention-aggregating platforms
viewpoints.description: McKinsey states that AI is fundamentally altering how advertising value is created, shifting it towards digital platforms that can influence consumer discovery, selection, and purchase. This transformation means success for marketers is less about securing data-driven impressions and more about being recommended by AI systems that shape what consumers see and buy, leading to a reallocation of ad spend. The value will concentrate with platforms effectively leveraging AI to guide consumer decisions.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: Established 'walled garden' platforms are well-positioned in new AI ad era
viewpoints.description: McKinsey identifies established 'walled garden' platforms as well-positioned to benefit from the new advertising era shaped by AI. These platforms, including TikTok, YouTube, and Meta, are strategically integrating AI agents and expanding into commerce offerings. Their ability to bundle discovery, buying, and measurement capabilities into single AI-managed products gives them a significant advantage, potentially controlling a larger share of consumer attention and transaction flows.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: Open web publishers face eroding economics from AI search disruption
viewpoints.description: McKinsey warns that the open web and traditional search are facing eroding economics due to AI's impact. With consumers increasingly comfortable with AI-generated answers and traditional search traffic declining, click-driven and scale-dependent publishing models are becoming unviable. Long-tail, SEO-dependent sites with limited user subscription models are particularly exposed to this shift, challenging their ability to monetize attention effectively in the evolving digital landscape.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: AI-native platforms emerging as significant challengers in discovery
viewpoints.description: McKinsey highlights that new AI-native platforms, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Claude, are rapidly expanding their share of consumer discovery. These platforms offer conversational AI interfaces and agent layers that consumers find faster and more useful for recommendations and synthesized answers, posing a direct challenge to traditional search engines. While they currently lack a mature advertising model, their privileged access to decision moments and behavioral data make them formidable emerging competitors.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

demand_drivers.driver: Integration of commerce and AI agents
demand_drivers.description: TikTok's strategy to expand beyond attention monetization by integrating commerce and AI agent offerings directly within its platform drives GMV.
Consumers are increasingly using platforms that combine discovery, purchasing, and measurement, leading to higher conversion rates through AI-enabled shopping experiences.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) from commerce on TikTok, a major social media and content sharing platform.
market_sizing.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

demand_drivers.description: AI shopping agents and other new applications are creating novel advertising opportunities, attracting additional media spend.
AI's ability to optimize targeting, planning, and creative generation is expected to boost ad campaign effectiveness, encouraging greater investment from advertisers.

market_sizing.methodology: Survey of advertisers indicating expectations for total media spend changes driven by AI. Three-quarters expect an increase, and one-third anticipate at least a 10% increase in Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) due to AI.
market_sizing.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action
